messages:
maya: FYI: our nightly SBOM/vuln run flagged libcurl CVE-2026-0458 in the runtime base (alpine:3.18). Exploit requires HTTP/2 and specific flags, but we should patch.
sam: Report: https://scans.internal/reports/184002 — shows info-leak vector. Severity: high for public-facing services.
leo: Which images use that base? I think gpu-workers, ephemeral-runner, and the model-sidecar.
maya: Correct. runtime-base owns it.
ops-jen: Heads-up: infra-oncall, we applied a KMS RBAC tightening last night — could affect image signing.
infra-oncall: Confirmed — removed `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign` from a few pipeline SAs as part of least-privilege.
sam: If signing is blocked CI will fail image promotion. We can either temporarily relax RBAC or use an alternative signing flow. Compliance prefers signed images.
leo: @sec-bot check for recent signing failures in logs.
sec-bot: Alert: signing failure at 2026-06-02T02:03Z for serviceAccount:image-pipeline@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com — error=PermissionDenied key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/image-signing
maya: Log excerpt:
```
ERROR signing: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = serviceAccount:image-pipeline@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com missing permission: cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign
```
compliance: We require audit trail of any temporary RBAC changes and SBOM + vuln diff uploaded to INC-4521.
ops-jen: Proposed safe plan: 1) Add a time-bound conditional binding for image-pipeline SA solely for sign permission 2) Run base-image rebuild with libcurl patched 3) Run SBOM + vuln scans 4) Deploy as canary then roll out 5) Revoke grant and document audit links. Thoughts?
sam: I can add a conditional binding with a strict expiration window: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood --member=serviceAccount:image-pipeline@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeySignerVerifier --condition='expression=request.time < timestamp("2026-06-02T06:00:00Z")'`
leo: When you add it, include an iam-change-audit label in the commit and set `audit-log:INC-4521` so it's easy to find.
ops-jen: Also, add SBOM-diff tag `sbom:libcurl-7.88.0` to the build.
maya: Kicking off build now: `ci/base-image/refresh --patch=libcurl-7.88.0 --ticket=INC-4521`
sec-bot: Build queued: job=ci-base-9876; logs -> https://ci.internal/jobs/ci-base-9876
infra-oncall: I'll tail KMS audit logs and confirm signing goes through.
ops-jen: Reminder: if signing still fails we can fallback to manual attest + notarization but that delays rollout. Temporary RBAC is faster.
maya: CI build: SUCCESS. Vuln scan: CVE-2026-0458 no longer present. SBOM updated.
sec-bot: Canary monitoring: 1h running, error rate stable, no regressions detected.
ops-jen: Revoking the temporary binding now and adding an audit note.
sam: Revoked. IAM change logged as `temporary-grant:image-pipeline:INC-4521`.
leo: Ticket updated with SBOM diff, vuln scan report, KMS audit links, and rollback plan. We'll write a short postmortem tomorrow documenting the RBAC window and approvals. :thumbsup:
compliance: Received. Please ensure the SBOM and scans are preserved in the evidence folder for the quarter.
maya: Closing the loop — canary promoted to 100%. Thanks everyone.
